1	"""Merge sort implementation for singly linked lists.
2	
3	Merge sort is well-suited for linked lists because, unlike arrays, it doesn't
4	need random access or extra copying — we sort by re-linking nodes in place.
5	
6	Time complexity:  O(n log n)  — the list is halved log n times, and each
7	                                 level of recursion does O(n) work merging.
8	Space complexity: O(log n)    — only the recursion stack; no auxiliary arrays.
9	"""
10	
11	
12	class Node:
13	    """A node in a singly linked list.
14	
15	    __slots__ is used to save memory by preventing the creation of a per-instance
16	    __dict__ — each Node only needs two fixed attributes.
17	    """
18	
19	    __slots__ = ("val", "next")
20	
21	    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
22	        self.val = val
23	        self.next = next
24	
25	
26	def split(head: Node) -> Node:
27	    """Find the middle of the list and split it into two halves.
28	
29	    Uses the classic slow/fast pointer technique:
30	      - 'slow' advances one node per step.
31	      - 'fast' advances two nodes per step.
32	      When fast reaches the end, slow is at (or just before) the midpoint.
33	
34	    We initialise fast to head.next (not head) so that in a two-node list
35	    [A, B], slow stays on A and we correctly split into [A] and [B].
36	
37	    After locating the midpoint we sever the link between the two halves
38	    (slow.next = None) so that each half is an independent, self-contained
39	    linked list that the recursive calls can sort independently.
40	
41	    Returns the head of the second (right) half.
42	    """
43	    slow, fast = head, head.next
44	
45	    # Walk fast two steps for every one step of slow.
46	    # The loop stops when fast reaches the end (None) or the last node.
47	    while fast and fast.next:
48	        slow = slow.next
49	        fast = fast.next.next
50	
51	    # slow.next is the first node of the right half.
52	    mid = slow.next
53	
54	    # Sever the link so the left half ends at 'slow'.
55	    slow.next = None
56	
57	    return mid
58	
59	
60	def merge(a: Node, b: Node) -> Node:
61	    """Merge two sorted linked lists into a single sorted linked list.
62	
63	    A dummy (sentinel) node is used as the starting point so we never have to
64	    special-case the very first insertion — every append is simply
65	    'tail.next = node'.
66	
67	    We compare the front nodes of each list, attach the smaller one to the
68	    merged list, and advance the pointer in that list.  When one list is
69	    exhausted, the remaining nodes of the other are already sorted, so we
70	    attach the whole remainder in one step (tail.next = a or b).
71	    """
72	    dummy = tail = Node(0)
73	
74	    # Walk both lists in lock-step, always picking the smaller front element.
75	    while a and b:
76	        if a.val <= b.val:
77	            tail.next, a = a, a.next
78	        else:
79	            tail.next, b = b, b.next
80	        tail = tail.next
81	
82	    # One list may still have leftover nodes — attach them as-is.
83	    tail.next = a or b
84	
85	    # Skip the dummy sentinel and return the real head.
86	    return dummy.next
87	
88	
89	def mergesort(head: Node) -> Node:
90	    """Sort a linked list in ascending order using merge sort.
91	
92	    The algorithm follows the classic divide-and-conquer pattern:
93	      1. BASE CASE — a list with 0 or 1 nodes is already sorted; return it.
94	      2. DIVIDE     — find the middle node and split the list into two halves.
95	      3. CONQUER    — recursively sort each half.
96	      4. COMBINE    — merge the two sorted halves into one sorted list.
97	
98	    Because we re-link existing nodes rather than creating new ones, the
99	    algorithm works in-place (aside from the O(log n) recursion stack).
100	    """
101	    # Base case: an empty list or a single node needs no sorting.
102	    if not head or not head.next:
103	        return head
104	
105	    # Step 1 — Split the list at the midpoint.
106	    mid = split(head)
107	
108	    # Step 2 — Recursively sort the left half (starting at head) and
109	    #          the right half (starting at mid).
110	    left = mergesort(head)
111	    right = mergesort(mid)
112	
113	    # Step 3 — Merge the two sorted halves and return the result.
114	    return merge(left, right)
115	
116	
117	# ── helpers for testing ──────────────────────────────────────────────
118	
119	def from_list(values):
120	    """Build a linked list from a plain Python list. Returns the head node."""
121	    dummy = tail = Node(0)
122	    for v in values:
123	        tail.next = Node(v)
124	        tail = tail.next
125	    return dummy.next
126	
127	
128	def to_list(head):
129	    """Collect linked list values into a plain Python list."""
130	    out = []
131	    while head:
132	        out.append(head.val)
133	        head = head.next
134	    return out

137	if __name__ == "__main__":
138	    tests = [
139	        [],
140	        [1],
141	        [2, 1],
142	        [3, 1, 2],
143	        [5, 4, 3, 2, 1],
144	        [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
145	        [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6],
146	    ]
147	    for t in tests:
148	        result = to_list(mergesort(from_list(t)))
149	        assert result == sorted(t), f"FAIL: {t} -> {result}"
150	        print(f"{t} -> {result}")
151	    print("All tests passed.")

40	
41	    Returns the head of the second (right) half.
42	    """
43	    slow, fast = head, head.next
44	
45	    # Walk fast two steps for every one step of slow.
46	    # The loop stops when fast reaches the end (None) or the last node.
47	    while fast and fast.next:
48	        slow = slow.next
49	        fast = fast.next.next
50	
51	    # slow.next is the first node of the right half.
52	    mid = slow.next
53	
54	    # Sever the link so the left half ends at 'slow'.
55	    slow.next = None
56	
57	    return mid
58	
59	
60	def merge(a: Node, b: Node) -> Node:
61	    """Merge two sorted linked lists into a single sorted linked list.
62	
63	    A dummy (sentinel) node is used as the starting point so we never have to
64	    special-case the very first insertion — every append is simply
65	    'tail.next = node'.
66	
67	    We compare the front nodes of each list, attach the smaller one to the
68	    merged list, and advance the pointer in that list.  When one list is
69	    exhausted, the remaining nodes of the other are already sorted, so we
70	    attach the whole remainder in one step (tail.next = a or b).
71	    """
72	    dummy = tail = Node(0)
73	
74	    # Walk both lists in lock-step, always picking the smaller front element.
75	    while a and b:
76	        if a.val <= b.val:
77	            tail.next, a = a, a.next
78	        else:
79	            tail.next, b = b, b.next
80	        tail = tail.next
81	
82	    # One list may still have leftover nodes — attach them as-is.
83	    tail.next = a or b
84	
85	    # Skip the dummy sentinel and return the real head.
86	    return dummy.next
87	
88	
89	def mergesort(head: Node) -> Node:
90	    """Sort a linked list in ascending order using merge sort.
91	
92	    The algorithm follows the classic divide-and-conquer pattern:
93	      1. BASE CASE — a list with 0 or 1 nodes is already sorted; return it.
94	      2. DIVIDE     — find the middle node and split the list into two halves.
95	      3. CONQUER    — recursively sort each half.
96	      4. COMBINE    — merge the two sorted halves into one sorted list.
97	
98	    Because we re-link existing nodes rather than creating new ones, the
99	    algorithm works in-place (aside from the O(log n) recursion stack).
100	    """
101	    # Base case: an empty list or a single node needs no sorting.
102	    if not head or not head.next:
103	        return head
104	
105	    # Step 1 — Split the list at the midpoint.
106	    mid = split(head)
107	
108	    # Step 2 — Recursively sort the left half (starting at head) and
109	    #          the right half (starting at mid).
110	    left = mergesort(head)
111	    right = mergesort(mid)
112	
113	    # Step 3 — Merge the two sorted halves and return the result.
114	    return merge(left, right)
115	
116	
117	# ── helpers for testing ──────────────────────────────────────────────
118	
119	def from_list(values):
120	    """Build a linked list from a plain Python list. Returns the head node."""
121	    dummy = tail = Node(0)
122	    for v in values:
123	        tail.next = Node(v)
124	        tail = tail.next
125	    return dummy.next
126	
127	
128	def to_list(head):
129	    """Collect linked list values into a plain Python list."""
130	    out = []
131	    while head:
132	        out.append(head.val)
133	        head = head.next
134	    return out

1	"""Probabilistic and classic data structures implemented from scratch."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import hashlib
6	import math
7	from typing import Any, Generic, TypeVar
8	
9	T = TypeVar("T")
10	K = TypeVar("K")
11	V = TypeVar("V")
12	
13	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
14	# HyperLogLog — cardinality estimation
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	
17	class HyperLogLog:
18	    """Probabilistic data structure for estimating the number of distinct elements.
19	
20	    Uses the HyperLogLog algorithm with harmonic-mean correction.
21	    Accuracy is controlled by *precision* (number of register bits):
22	    standard error ≈ 1.04 / sqrt(2**precision).
23	
24	    Supports ``add`` and ``count`` — not stack-like operations.
25	    """
26	
27	    def __init__(self, precision: int = 14) -> None:
28	        if not 4 <= precision <= 16:
29	            raise ValueError("precision must be between 4 and 16")
30	        self.precision = precision
31	        self.num_registers = 1 << precision
32	        self.registers: list[int] = [0] * self.num_registers
33	
34	    def _hash(self, element: Any) -> int:
35	        digest = hashlib.sha256(str(element).encode()).digest()
36	        return int.from_bytes(digest, "big")
37	
38	    def add(self, element: Any) -> None:
39	        """Add an element to the sketch."""
40	        h = self._hash(element)
41	        register_index = h >> (256 - self.precision)
42	        remaining = h & ((1 << (256 - self.precision)) - 1)
43	        leading_zeros = self._count_leading_zeros(remaining, 256 - self.precision) + 1
44	        self.registers[register_index] = max(self.registers[register_index], leading_zeros)
45	
46	    def count(self) -> int:
47	        """Estimate the number of distinct elements added."""
48	        alpha = self._alpha()
49	        raw = alpha * self.num_registers**2 / sum(2.0**-r for r in self.registers)
50	
51	        if raw <= 2.5 * self.num_registers:
52	            zeros = self.registers.count(0)
53	            if zeros:
54	                return int(self.num_registers * math.log(self.num_registers / zeros))
55	        return int(raw)
56	
57	    def merge(self, other: HyperLogLog) -> HyperLogLog:
58	        """Return a new HyperLogLog that is the union of *self* and *other*."""
59	        if self.precision != other.precision:
60	            raise ValueError("cannot merge sketches with different precision")
61	        merged = HyperLogLog(self.precision)
62	        merged.registers = [max(a, b) for a, b in zip(self.registers, other.registers)]
63	        return merged
64	
65	    def __len__(self) -> int:
66	        return self.count()
67	
68	    def __contains__(self, element: Any) -> bool:
69	        raise NotImplementedError(
70	            "HyperLogLog does not support membership testing; use count() instead"
71	        )
72	
73	    # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------------
74	
75	    @staticmethod
76	    def _count_leading_zeros(value: int, width: int) -> int:
77	        if value == 0:
78	            return width
79	        return width - value.bit_length()
80	
81	    def _alpha(self) -> float:
82	        if self.num_registers == 16:
83	            return 0.673
84	        if self.num_registers == 32:
85	            return 0.697
86	        if self.num_registers == 64:
87	            return 0.709
88	        return 0.7213 / (1 + 1.079 / self.num_registers)
89	
90	
91	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	# Stack — LIFO
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	
95	class Stack(Generic[T]):
96	    """LIFO stack with O(1) push, pop, and peek.
97	
98	    Backed by a dynamic array (Python list).
99	    """
100	
101	    def __init__(self) -> None:
102	        self._data: list[T] = []
103	
104	    def push(self, item: T) -> None:
105	        """Push *item* onto the top of the stack."""
106	        self._data.append(item)
107	
108	    def pop(self) -> T:
109	        """Remove and return the top item.
110	
111	        Raises
112	        ------
113	        IndexError
114	            If the stack is empty.
115	        """
116	        if self.is_empty():
117	            raise IndexError("pop from empty stack")
118	        return self._data.pop()
119	
120	    def peek(self) -> T:
121	        """Return the top item without removing it.
122	
123	        Raises
124	        ------
125	        IndexError
126	            If the stack is empty.
127	        """
128	        if self.is_empty():
129	            raise IndexError("peek from empty stack")
130	        return self._data[-1]
131	
132	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
133	        """Return ``True`` if the stack has no items."""
134	        return len(self._data) == 0
135	
136	    def __len__(self) -> int:
137	        return len(self._data)
138	
139	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
140	        return f"Stack({self._data})"
141	
142	
143	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	# HashMap — O(1) average put / get / remove
145	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146	
147	class HashMap(Generic[K, V]):
148	    """Hash map with separate chaining, O(1) average-case operations.
149	
150	    Automatically resizes when the load factor exceeds 0.75.
151	    """
152	
153	    _INITIAL_CAPACITY = 16
154	    _LOAD_FACTOR_THRESHOLD = 0.75
155	
156	    def __init__(self) -> None:
157	        self._capacity = self._INITIAL_CAPACITY
158	        self._buckets: list[list[tuple[K, V]]] = [[] for _ in range(self._capacity)]
159	        self._size = 0
160	
161	    # -- public API -----------------------------------------------------------
162	
163	    def put(self, key: K, value: V) -> None:
164	        """Insert or update the *key* → *value* mapping."""
165	        if self._load_factor() >= self._LOAD_FACTOR_THRESHOLD:
166	            self._resize(self._capacity * 2)
167	
168	        bucket = self._bucket_for(key)
169	        for i, (k, _) in enumerate(bucket):
170	            if k == key:
171	                bucket[i] = (key, value)
172	                return
173	        bucket.append((key, value))
174	        self._size += 1
175	
176	    def get(self, key: K, default: V | None = None) -> V | None:
177	        """Return the value for *key*, or *default* if not found."""
178	        for k, v in self._bucket_for(key):
179	            if k == key:
180	                return v
181	        return default
182	
183	    def remove(self, key: K) -> V:
184	        """Remove and return the value for *key*.
185	
186	        Raises
187	        ------
188	        KeyError
189	            If *key* is not in the map.
190	        """
191	        bucket = self._bucket_for(key)
192	        for i, (k, v) in enumerate(bucket):
193	            if k == key:
194	                del bucket[i]
195	                self._size -= 1
196	                return v
197	        raise KeyError(key)
198	
199	    def contains(self, key: K) -> bool:
200	        """Return ``True`` if *key* is in the map."""
201	        return any(k == key for k, _ in self._bucket_for(key))
202	
203	    def __len__(self) -> int:
204	        return self._size
205	
206	    def __contains__(self, key: K) -> bool:
207	        return self.contains(key)
208	
209	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
210	        items = ", ".join(f"{k!r}: {v!r}" for bucket in self._buckets for k, v in bucket)
211	        return f"HashMap({{{items}}})"
212	
213	    # -- internals ------------------------------------------------------------
214	
215	    def _bucket_for(self, key: K) -> list[tuple[K, V]]:
216	        return self._buckets[hash(key) % self._capacity]
217	
218	    def _load_factor(self) -> float:
219	        return self._size / self._capacity
220	
221	    def _resize(self, new_capacity: int) -> None:
222	        old_buckets = self._buckets
223	        self._capacity = new_capacity
224	        self._buckets = [[] for _ in range(self._capacity)]
225	        self._size = 0
226	        for bucket in old_buckets:
227	            for key, value in bucket:
228	                self.put(key, value)

3	
4	import sys
5	import statistics
6	from pathlib import Path
7	
8	import pandas as pd
9	
10	
11	def load_parquet(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
12	    df = pd.read_parquet(path)
13	    # Drop columns that are entirely NaN
14	    df = df.dropna(axis=1, how="all")

16	
17	
18	def coerce_numeric(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
19	    """Convert a series to numeric, coercing errors to NaN."""
20	    return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce")
21	
22	
23	def compute_stats(series: pd.Series) -> dict:
24	    """Compute mean, median, and standard deviation for a numeric series."""
25	    clean = series.dropna()
26	    if clean.empty:
27	        return {"count": 0, "mean": None, "median": None, "std_dev": None}
28	    return {
29	        "count": len(clean),
30	        "mean": round(clean.mean(), 2),
31	        "median": round(clean.median(), 2),
32	        "std_dev": round(clean.std(), 2),
33	    }
34	
35	
36	def group_by_category(df: pd.DataFrame, cat_col: str, val_col: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
37	    """Group by a categorical column and compute stats for a numeric column."""
38	    temp = df[[cat_col, val_col]].copy()
39	    temp[val_col] = coerce_numeric(temp[val_col])
40	    temp = temp.dropna(subset=[val_col, cat_col])
41	
42	    rows = []
43	    for group, subset in temp.groupby(cat_col):
44	        vals = subset[val_col]
45	        rows.append({
46	            cat_col: group,
47	            "count": len(vals),
48	            "mean": round(vals.mean(), 2),
49	            "median": round(vals.median(), 2),
50	            "std_dev": round(vals.std(), 2),
51	            "min": round(vals.min(), 2),
52	            "max": round(vals.max(), 2),
53	        })
54	    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("count", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
55	
56	
57	def build_report(path: str) -> str:
58	    df = load_parquet(path)
59	    lines = []
60	    lines.append("=" * 70)
61	    lines.append(f"  PARQUET DATA ANALYSIS REPORT")
62	    lines.append(f"  Source: {path}")
63	    lines.append("=" * 70)
64	
65	    # --- Overview ---
66	    lines.append(f"\nOVERVIEW")
67	    lines.append(f"  Rows: {len(df)}")
68	    lines.append(f"  Columns: {len(df.columns)}")
69	    lines.append(f"  Column names: {', '.join(df.columns)}")
70	
71	    # --- Identify column types ---
72	    numeric_cols = []
73	    categorical_cols = []
74	    for col in df.columns:
75	        coerced = coerce_numeric(df[col])
76	        if coerced.notna().sum() > 0:
77	            numeric_cols.append(col)
78	        else:
79	            categorical_cols.append(col)
80	
81	    lines.append(f"\n  Numeric columns:     {', '.join(numeric_cols) or 'none'}")
82	    lines.append(f"  Categorical columns: {', '.join(categorical_cols) or 'none'}")
83	
84	    # --- Per-column statistics ---
85	    lines.append(f"\n{'─' * 70}")
86	    lines.append("COLUMN STATISTICS")
87	    lines.append(f"{'─' * 70}")
88	
89	    for col in numeric_cols:
90	        stats = compute_stats(coerce_numeric(df[col]))
91	        lines.append(f"\n  {col}:")
92	        lines.append(f"    Count:      {stats['count']}")
93	        lines.append(f"    Mean:       {stats['mean']}")
94	        lines.append(f"    Median:     {stats['median']}")
95	        lines.append(f"    Std Dev:    {stats['std_dev']}")
96	
97	    for col in categorical_cols:

99	        lines.append(f"\n  {col}:")
100	        lines.append(f"    Non-null:   {df[col].notna().sum()}")
101	        lines.append(f"    Unique:     {df[col].nunique()}")
102	        lines.append(f"    Top values:")
103	        for val, cnt in vc.head(5).items():
104	            lines.append(f"      {val}: {cnt}")
105	
106	    # --- Group-by analysis ---
107	    # Find a categorical column to group by and a numeric column to aggregate
108	    group_col = None
109	    for col in categorical_cols:
110	        if df[col].nunique() <= 20:
111	            group_col = col
112	            break
113	    if group_col is None and categorical_cols:

115

117	        lines.append(f"\n{'─' * 70}")

119	        lines.append(f"{'─' * 70}")
120	
121	        for val_col in numeric_cols:

123	            lines.append(f"\n  Aggregated by '{group_col}' for column '{val_col}':\n")

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""CSV data analyzer: computes statistics, groups by categories, and generates a summary report."""
3	
4	import csv
5	import sys
6	import statistics
7	from collections import defaultdict
8	
9	
10	def read_csv(filepath):
11	    with open(filepath, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
12	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
13	        return list(reader)
14	
15	
16	def is_numeric(value):
17	    try:
18	        float(value)
19	        return True
20	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
21	        return False
22	
23	
24	def compute_stats(values):
25	    nums = [float(v) for v in values if is_numeric(v)]
26	    if not nums:
27	        return None
28	    return {
29	        "count": len(nums),
30	        "mean": statistics.mean(nums),
31	        "median": statistics.median(nums),
32	        "stdev": statistics.stdev(nums) if len(nums) > 1 else 0.0,
33	        "min": min(nums),
34	        "max": max(nums),
35	    }
36	
37	
38	def format_stat(key, val):
39	    if isinstance(val, float):
40	        return f"  {key:<10} {val:>12.4f}"
41	    return f"  {key:<10} {val:>12}"
42	
43	
44	def analyze_csv(filepath, group_by=None):
45	    rows = read_csv(filepath)
46	    if not rows:
47	        print("No data found.")
48	        return
49	
50	    columns = list(rows[0].keys())
51	    numeric_cols = [c for c in columns if all(is_numeric(r[c]) for r in rows)]
52	    categorical_cols = [c for c in columns if c not in numeric_cols]
53	
54	    if not numeric_cols:
55	        print("No numeric columns found.")
56	        return
57	
58	    print(f"{'='*60}")
59	    print(f" CSV Analysis Report: {filepath}")
60	    print(f"{'='*60}")
61	    print(f" Rows: {len(rows)}")
62	    print(f" Columns: {len(columns)} ({', '.join(columns)})")
63	    print(f" Numeric: {', '.join(numeric_cols)}")
64	    print(f" Categorical: {', '.join(categorical_cols) or 'none'}")
65	    print()
66	
67	    # Overall statistics per numeric column
68	    print(f"{'─'*60}")
69	    print(" Overall Statistics")
70	    print(f"{'─'*60}")
71	    for col in numeric_cols:
72	        stats = compute_stats([r[col] for r in rows])
73	        print(f"\n [{col}]")
74	        for k, v in stats.items():
75	            print(format_stat(k, v))
76	    print()
77	
78	    # Group-by analysis
79	    if group_by and group_by in columns:
80	        groups = defaultdict(list)
81	        for row in rows:
82	            groups[row[group_by]].append(row)
83	
84	        print(f"{'─'*60}")
85	        print(f" Grouped by: {group_by} ({len(groups)} groups)")
86	        print(f"{'─'*60}")
87	
88	        for group_name in sorted(groups.keys()):
89	            group_rows = groups[group_name]
90	            print(f"\n ▸ {group_by}={group_name}  (n={len(group_rows)})")
91	            for col in numeric_cols:
92	                stats = compute_stats([r[col] for r in group_rows])
93	                if stats:
94	                    print(f"   {col}: mean={stats['mean']:.4f}  "
95	                          f"median={stats['median']:.4f}  stdev={stats['stdev']:.4f}")
96	        print()
97	
98	    # Value counts for categorical columns
99	    if categorical_cols:
100	        print(f"{'─'*60}")
101	        print(" Categorical Value Counts")
102	        print(f"{'─'*60}")
103	        for col in categorical_cols:
104	            counts = defaultdict(int)
105	            for row in rows:
106	                counts[row[col]] += 1
107	            print(f"\n [{col}]")
108	            for val, cnt in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
109	                print(f"   {val:<30} {cnt}")
110	        print()
111	
112	    print(f"{'='*60}")
113	    print(" End of Report")
114	    print(f"{'='*60}")
115	
116	
117	def main():
118	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
119	        print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <csv_file> [--group-by <column>]")
120	        sys.exit(1)
121	
122	    filepath = sys.argv[1]
123	    group_by = None
124	    if "--group-by" in sys.argv:
125	        idx = sys.argv.index("--group-by")
126	        if idx + 1 < len(sys.argv):
127	            group_by = sys.argv[idx + 1]
128	
129	    analyze_csv(filepath, group_by)
130	
131	
132	if __name__ == "__main__":
133	    main()

3	import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
4	import statistics
5	import sys

7	from pathlib import Path

9	
10	def parse_xml(filepath):
11	    """Parse XML file and return list of records as dicts."""

13	    root = tree.getroot()
14	    records = []
15	    for item in root:

17	        for child in item:
18	            record[child.tag] = child.text

20	    return records
21	
22	
23	def coerce_numeric(value):
24	    """Try to convert a string to float; return None if not numeric."""
25	    try:
26	        return float(value)
27	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
28	        return None
29	
30	
31	def compute_stats(values):
32	    """Compute descriptive statistics for a list of numeric values."""
33	    if not values:
34	        return {}
35	    return {
36	        "count": len(values),
37	        "mean": round(statistics.mean(values), 4),
38	        "median": round(statistics.median(values), 4),
39	        "stdev": round(statistics.stdev(values), 4) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0,
40	        "min": min(values),
41	        "max": max(values),
42	    }
43	
44	
45	def analyze(records, category_field, value_field):
46	    """Group records by category_field, compute stats on value_field."""
47	    groups = defaultdict(list)
48	    ungrouped = []
49	
50	    for rec in records:
51	        cat = rec.get(category_field, "Unknown")
52	        val = coerce_numeric(rec.get(value_field))
53	        if val is not None:
54	            groups[cat].append(val)
55	        else:
56	            ungrouped.append(rec)
57	
58	    results = {}
59	    for cat in sorted(groups):
60	        results[cat] = compute_stats(groups[cat])
61	
62	    return results, ungrouped
63	
64

68	    lines.append("=" * 60)

70	    lines.append("=" * 60)

73	    lines.append(f"  Groups found   : {len(results)}")

78	        all_values.extend([st["mean"]] * st["count"])  # approximate for overall

82	        lines.append(f"    Count  : {st['count']}")
83	        lines.append(f"    Mean   : {st['mean']}")
84	        lines.append(f"    Median : {st['median']}")
85	        lines.append(f"    StdDev : {st['stdev']}")
86	        lines.append(f"    Min    : {st['min']}")
87	        lines.append(f"    Max    : {st['max']}")
88	        lines.append("")
89	
90	    if ungrouped:
91	        lines.append(f"  Skipped {len(ungrouped)} non-numeric record(s).")
92	        lines.append("")
93	
94	    lines.append("=" * 60)
95	    return "\n".join(lines)
96	
97	
98	def main():
99	    if len(sys.argv) < 4:
100	        print("Usage: python xml_analyzer.py <file.xml> <category_field> <value_field>")
101	        print("Example: python xml_analyzer.py data.xml category price")
102	        sys.exit(1)
103	
104	    filepath = sys.argv[1]
105	    category_field = sys.argv[2]
106	    value_field = sys.argv[3]
107	
108	    if not Path(filepath).exists():
109	        print(f"Error: file '{filepath}' not found.")
110	        sys.exit(1)
111	
112	    records = parse_xml(filepath)
113	    print(f"Parsed {len(records)} record(s) from {filepath}")
114	
115	    results, ungrouped = analyze(records, category_field, value_field)
116	    report = generate_report(results, ungrouped, category_field, value_field)
117	    print(report)
118	
119	    report_path = Path(filepath).with_suffix(".report.txt")
120	    report_path.write_text(report)
121	    print(f"Report saved to {report_path}")
122	
123	
124	if __name__ == "__main__":
125	    main()

1	"""Analyze Excel data: compute statistics, group by categories, generate summary report."""
2	
3	import sys
4	from pathlib import Path
5	
6	import pandas as pd
7	
8	
9	def load_data(filepath: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
10	    """Load Excel or CSV file into a DataFrame."""
11	    path = Path(filepath)
12	    if path.suffix in (".xlsx", ".xls"):
13	        return pd.read_excel(filepath)
14	    if path.suffix == ".csv":
15	        return pd.read_csv(filepath)
16	    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file format: {path.suffix}")
17	
18	
19	def compute_statistics(df: pd.DataFrame, numeric_cols: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
20	    """Compute mean, median, and standard deviation for numeric columns."""
21	    stats = pd.DataFrame({
22	        "mean": df[numeric_cols].mean(),
23	        "median": df[numeric_cols].median(),
24	        "std_dev": df[numeric_cols].std(),
25	        "min": df[numeric_cols].min(),
26	        "max": df[numeric_cols].max(),
27	        "count": df[numeric_cols].count(),
28	    })
29	    return stats.round(4)
30	
31	
32	def group_by_category(
33	    df: pd.DataFrame, category_col: str, numeric_cols: list[str]
34	) -> pd.DataFrame:
35	    """Group data by a categorical column and compute aggregated statistics."""
36	    grouped = df.groupby(category_col)[numeric_cols].agg(["mean", "median", "std", "count"])
37	    # Flatten multi-level column names
38	    grouped.columns = [f"{col}_{stat}" for col, stat in grouped.columns]
39	    return grouped.round(4)
40	
41	
42	def generate_report(
43	    df: pd.DataFrame,
44	    overall_stats: pd.DataFrame,
45	    grouped_stats: pd.DataFrame,
46	    category_col: str,
47	    output_path: str,
48	) -> None:
49	    """Write a summary report to a text file."""
50	    lines = []
51	    lines.append("=" * 60)
52	    lines.append("DATA ANALYSIS SUMMARY REPORT")
53	    lines.append("=" * 60)
54	    lines.append(f"\nTotal rows: {len(df)}")
55	    lines.append(f"Total columns: {len(df.columns)}")
56	    lines.append(f"Category column: {category_col}")
57	    lines.append(f"Number of categories: {df[category_col].nunique()}")
58	
59	    lines.append("\n" + "-" * 60)
60	    lines.append("OVERALL STATISTICS (numeric columns)")
61	    lines.append("-" * 60)
62	    lines.append(overall_stats.to_string())
63	
64	    lines.append("\n" + "-" * 60)
65	    lines.append(f"STATISTICS GROUPED BY '{category_col}'")
66	    lines.append("-" * 60)
67	    lines.append(grouped_stats.to_string())
68	
69	    lines.append("\n" + "=" * 60)
70	
71	    report = "\n".join(lines)
72	    Path(output_path).write_text(report)
73	    print(report)
74	    print(f"\nReport saved to: {output_path}")
75	
76	
77	def main() -> None:
78	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
79	        print("Usage: python analyze_excel.py <file.xlsx|file.csv> [category_column] [output_report.txt]")
80	        print("\nExample:")
81	        print("  python analyze_excel.py sales.xlsx Region report.txt")
82	        sys.exit(1)
83	
84	    filepath = sys.argv[1]
85	    output_path = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "summary_report.txt"
86	
87	    # Load data
88	    print(f"Loading {filepath}...")
89	    df = load_data(filepath)
90	    print(f"Loaded {len(df)} rows x {len(df.columns)} columns\n")
91	
92	    # Identify numeric columns
93	    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include="number").columns.tolist()
94	    if not numeric_cols:
95	        print("Error: no numeric columns found in the data.")
96	        sys.exit(1)
97	
98	    # Determine category column
99	    if len(sys.argv) > 2:
100	        category_col = sys.argv[2]
101	    else:
102	        categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=["object", "category"]).columns.tolist()
103	        if not categorical_cols:
104	            print("No categorical columns found. Generating report without grouping.")
105	            # Use a dummy constant column so grouping still works
106	            df["_all"] = "all"
107	            category_col = "_all"
108	        else:
109	            category_col = categorical_cols[0]
110	            print(f"Auto-selected category column: '{category_col}'")
111	
112	    if category_col not in df.columns:
113	        print(f"Error: column '{category_col}' not found. Available columns: {list(df.columns)}")
114	        sys.exit(1)
115	
116	    # Compute
117	    overall_stats = compute_statistics(df, numeric_cols)
118	    grouped_stats = group_by_category(df, category_col, numeric_cols)
119	
120	    # Report
121	    generate_report(df, overall_stats, grouped_stats, category_col, output_path)
122	
123	
124	if __name__ == "__main__":
125	    main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""CSV data cleaning pipeline that reads, cleans, and outputs a Markdown table.
3	
4	Cleaning steps:
5	  1. Drop rows where all values are missing
6	  2. Remove exact duplicate rows
7	  3. Strip whitespace from string columns
8	  4. Convert numeric columns to proper types (int/float)
9	  5. Parse date-like columns to ISO format
10	  6. Fill remaining missing values (numeric → median, string → "N/A")
11	
12	Usage:
13	    python csv_clean_pipeline.py input.csv [-o output.md] [--fill-strategy median|mean|drop]
14	"""
15	
16	import argparse
17	import csv
18	import re
19	import sys
20	from collections import defaultdict
21	from datetime import datetime
22	from statistics import median, mean
23	
24	
25	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	# Type detection helpers
27	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	
29	_INT_RE = re.compile(r"^-?\d+$")
30	_FLOAT_RE = re.compile(r"^-?\d+\.\d+$")
31	_DATE_FORMATS = [
32	    "%Y-%m-%d",
33	    "%m/%d/%Y",
34	    "%d-%m-%Y",
35	    "%Y/%m/%d",
36	    "%b %d, %Y",
37	]
38	
39	
40	def _is_int(v: str) -> bool:
41	    return bool(_INT_RE.match(v.strip()))
42	
43	
44	def _is_float(v: str) -> bool:
45	    return bool(_FLOAT_RE.match(v.strip()))
46	
47	
48	def _parse_date(v: str):
49	    """Try common date formats; return ISO string or None."""
50	    v = v.strip()
51	    for fmt in _DATE_FORMATS:
52	        try:
53	            return datetime.strptime(v, fmt).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
54	        except ValueError:
55	            continue
56	    return None
57	
58	
59	def _detect_column_type(values: list[str]) -> str:
60	    """Return 'int', 'float', 'date', or 'str' based on non-empty values."""
61	    non_empty = [v for v in values if v.strip()]
62	    if not non_empty:
63	        return "str"
64	
65	    if all(_is_int(v) for v in non_empty):
66	        return "int"
67	    if all(_is_float(v) for v in non_empty):
68	        return "float"
69	    if all(_parse_date(v) is not None for v in non_empty):
70	        return "date"
71	    return "str"
72	
73	
74	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75	# Cleaning functions
76	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	
78	def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict[str, str]]]:
79	    """Read CSV and return (headers, rows) where rows are ordered dicts."""
80	    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
81	        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
82	        headers = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
83	        rows = [dict(row) for row in reader]
84	    return headers, rows
85

2	"""Analyze YAML data: compute statistics, group by categories, generate summary report."""
3	
4	import sys
5	import yaml
6	import statistics
7	from collections import defaultdict
8	from pathlib import Path
9	
10	
11	def load_yaml(path):
12	    with open(path) as f:
13	        return yaml.safe_load(f)
14	
15	
16	def compute_stats(values):
17	    if len(values) < 2:
18	        return {"count": len(values), "mean": values[0] if values else 0}
19	    return {
20	        "count": len(values),
21	        "mean": round(statistics.mean(values), 4),
22	        "median": round(statistics.median(values), 4),
23	        "std_dev": round(statistics.stdev(values), 4),
24	        "min": min(values),
25	        "max": max(values),
26	    }
27	
28	
29	def extract_numeric_fields(records):
30	    """Find all numeric fields across records and group their values."""
31	    field_values = defaultdict(list)
32	    for record in records:
33	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
34	            continue
35	        for key, val in record.items():
36	            if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
37	                field_values[key].append(val)
38	    return field_values
39	
40	
41	def group_by(records, key):
42	    """Group records by a categorical field."""
43	    groups = defaultdict(list)
44	    for record in records:
45	        if isinstance(record, dict) and key in record:
46	            groups[record[key]].append(record)
47	    return dict(groups)
48	
49	
50	def generate_report(data, category_field=None):
51	    lines = []
52	    lines.append("=" * 60)
53	    lines.append("YAML DATA ANALYSIS REPORT")
54	    lines.append("=" * 60)
55	
56	    # Normalize: accept a list directly or a dict with a list under a key
57	    if isinstance(data, list):
58	        records = data
59	    elif isinstance(data, dict):
60	        # Pick the first key whose value is a list
61	        for v in data.values():
62	            if isinstance(v, list):
63	                records = v
64	                break
65	        else:
66	            records = [data]
67	    else:
68	        return "Error: unsupported YAML structure"
69	
70	    lines.append(f"\nTotal records: {len(records)}")
71	
72	    # --- Overall statistics for numeric fields ---
73	    field_values = extract_numeric_fields(records)
74	    if field_values:
75	        lines.append("\n" + "-" * 60)
76	        lines.append("OVERALL NUMERIC STATISTICS")
77	        lines.append("-" * 60)
78	        for field, values in sorted(field_values.items()):
79	            stats = compute_stats(values)
80	            lines.append(f"\n  {field}:")
81	            for k, v in stats.items():
82	                lines.append(f"    {k:>8}: {v}")
83	
84	    # --- Group-by analysis ---
85	    if category_field and records:
86	        groups = group_by(records, category_field)
87	        if groups:
88	            lines.append("\n" + "-" * 60)
89	            lines.append(f"GROUPED BY '{category_field}' ({len(groups)} groups)")
90	            lines.append("-" * 60)
91	            for group_name, group_records in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda x: str(x[0])):
92	                lines.append(f"\n  [{group_name}] ({len(group_records)} records)")
93	                grp_field_values = extract_numeric_fields(group_records)
94	                for field, values in sorted(grp_field_values.items()):
95	                    stats = compute_stats(values)
96	                    lines.append(f"    {field}: mean={stats['mean']}, median={stats['median']}, std_dev={stats.get('std_dev', 'N/A')}")
97	
98	    lines.append("\n" + "=" * 60)
99	    return "\n".join(lines)
100	
101	
102	def main():
103	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
104	        print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <data.yaml> [category_field]")
105	        print(f"  category_field: optional field name to group records by")
106	        sys.exit(1)
107	
108	    path = sys.argv[1]
109	    category = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
110	
111	    data = load_yaml(path)
112	    report = generate_report(data, category_field=category)
113	    print(report)
114	
115	
116	if __name__ == "__main__":
117	    main()

220	        print(f"Saved {len(rows)} rows to {output}", file=sys.stderr)
221	    else:
222	        writer = csv.DictWriter(sys.stdout, fieldnames=columns, extrasaction="ignore")
223	        writer.writeheader()
224	        for row in rows:

1	"""Merge multiple XML files based on a common key column."""
2	
3	import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
4	from collections import OrderedDict
5	
6	
7	def merge_xml_files(file_paths, key_tag, root_tag="data", row_tag="row"):
8	    """Merge multiple XML files by joining rows on a common key tag.
9	
10	    Each XML file is expected to have the structure:
11	        <root_tag>
12	            <row_tag>
13	                <key_tag>value</key_tag>
14	                <other_tag>...</other_tag>
15	            </row_tag>
16	        </root_tag>
17	
18	    Rows from later files extend rows from earlier files. If a key appears in
19	    multiple files, tags from later files overwrite same-name tags from earlier
20	    files; new tags are added.
21	
22	    Args:
23	        file_paths: List of paths to XML files.
24	        key_tag: The child element tag used as the join key.
25	        root_tag: Tag name of the root element (default "data").
26	        row_tag: Tag name of each row element (default "row").
27	
28	    Returns:
29	        An xml.etree.ElementTree.Element containing the merged rows.
30	    """
31	    merged = OrderedDict()  # key_value -> OrderedDict of {tag: text}
32	
33	    for path in file_paths:
34	        tree = ET.parse(path)
35	        root = tree.getroot()
36	        for row in root.findall(row_tag):
37	            key_el = row.find(key_tag)
38	            if key_el is None:
39	                continue
40	            key_value = key_el.text
41	
42	            if key_value not in merged:
43	                merged[key_value] = OrderedDict()
44	
45	            for child in row:
46	                merged[key_value][child.tag] = child.text
47	
48	    # Build the merged XML tree
49	    new_root = ET.Element(root_tag)
50	    for key_value, fields in merged.items():
51	        row_el = ET.SubElement(new_root, row_tag)
52	        for tag, text in fields.items():
53	            child = ET.SubElement(row_el, tag)
54	            child.text = text
55	
56	    return new_root
57	
58	
59	def merge_xml_files_to_string(file_paths, key_tag, **kwargs):
60	    """Same as merge_xml_files but returns the result as an XML string."""
61	    root = merge_xml_files(file_paths, key_tag, **kwargs)
62	    return ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
63	
64	
65	if __name__ == "__main__":
66	    import sys
67	
68	    if len(sys.argv) < 4:
69	        print("Usage: python merge_xml.py <key_tag> <output.xml> <input1.xml> [input2.xml ...]")
70	        sys.exit(1)
71	
72	    key = sys.argv[1]
73	    output = sys.argv[2]
74	    inputs = sys.argv[3:]
75	
76	    merged_root = merge_xml_files(inputs, key)
77	    tree = ET.ElementTree(merged_root)
78	    ET.indent(tree, space="  ")
79	    tree.write(output, xml_declaration=True, encoding="unicode")
80	    print(f"Merged {len(inputs)} file(s) -> {output}")
81

1	"""Min-heap from scratch with all standard operations.
2	
3	Supports: insert, extract_min, peek, decrease_key, delete,
4	build_heap, merge, and standard dunder methods.
5	"""
6	
7	
8	class MinHeap:
9	    __slots__ = ("_heap", "_pos")
10	
11	    def __init__(self, items=None):
12	        self._heap: list[list] = []  # [key, value] pairs
13	        self._pos: dict = {}  # value -> index in _heap
14	        if items is not None:
15	            self.build_heap(items)
16	
17	    # ── Query ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
18	
19	    def peek(self):
20	        """Return (key, value) of the minimum element. O(1)."""
21	        if not self._heap:
22	            raise IndexError("peek from empty heap")
23	        return tuple(self._heap[0])
24	
25	    def __len__(self) -> int:
26	        return len(self._heap)
27	
28	    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
29	        return bool(self._heap)
30	
31	    def __contains__(self, value) -> bool:
32	        return value in self._pos
33	
34	    # ── Insert ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	
36	    def insert(self, value, key) -> None:
37	        """Insert an item with the given key (priority). O(log n)."""
38	        idx = len(self._heap)
39	        self._heap.append([key, value])
40	        self._pos[value] = idx
41	        self._sift_up(idx)
42	
43	    # ── Extract ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	
45	    def extract_min(self):
46	        """Remove and return (key, value) of the minimum element. O(log n)."""
47	        if not self._heap:
48	            raise IndexError("extract from empty heap")
49	        self._swap(0, len(self._heap) - 1)
50	        key, value = self._heap.pop()
51	        del self._pos[value]
52	        if self._heap:
53	            self._sift_down(0)
54	        return (key, value)
55	
56	    # ── Decrease key ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57	
58	    def decrease_key(self, value, new_key) -> None:
59	        """Decrease the key of the given value. O(log n)."""
60	        if value not in self._pos:
61	            raise KeyError(f"value {value!r} not in heap")
62	        idx = self._pos[value]
63	        if new_key > self._heap[idx][0]:
64	            raise ValueError("new key is greater than current key")
65	        self._heap[idx][0] = new_key
66	        self._sift_up(idx)
67	
68	    # ── Delete ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69	
70	    def delete(self, value) -> None:
71	        """Remove an arbitrary value from the heap. O(log n)."""
72	        if value not in self._pos:
73	            raise KeyError(f"value {value!r} not in heap")
74	        idx = self._pos[value]
75	        last = len(self._heap) - 1
76	        if idx != last:
77	            self._swap(idx, last)
78	            self._heap.pop()
79	            del self._pos[value]
80	            if idx < len(self._heap):
81	                parent = (idx - 1) // 2
82	                if idx > 0 and self._heap[idx][0] < self._heap[parent][0]:
83	                    self._sift_up(idx)
84	                else:
85	                    self._sift_down(idx)
86	        else:
87	            self._heap.pop()
88	            del self._pos[value]
89	
90	    # ── Build heap ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
91	
92	    def build_heap(self, items) -> None:
93	        """Build a heap from an iterable of (value, key) pairs. O(n)."""
94	        self._heap = [[k, v] for v, k in items]
95	        self._pos = {v: i for i, (k, v) in enumerate(self._heap)}
96	        for i in range(len(self._heap) // 2 - 1, -1, -1):
97	            self._sift_down(i)
98	
99	    # ── Merge ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
100	
101	    def merge(self, other: "MinHeap") -> "MinHeap":
102	        """Return a new MinHeap containing elements from both heaps. O(n)."""
103	        combined = []
104	        for key, value in self._heap:
105	            combined.append((value, key))
106	        for key, value in other._heap:
107	            combined.append((value, key))
108	        return MinHeap(combined)
109	
110	    # ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
111	
112	    def _swap(self, i, j) -> None:
113	        self._heap[i], self._heap[j] = self._heap[j], self._heap[i]
114	        self._pos[self._heap[i][1]] = i
115	        self._pos[self._heap[j][1]] = j
116	
117	    def _sift_up(self, i) -> None:
118	        heap = self._heap
119	        while i > 0:
120	            parent = (i - 1) // 2
121	            if heap[i][0] < heap[parent][0]:
122	                self._swap(i, parent)
123	                i = parent
124	            else:
125	                break
126	
127	    def _sift_down(self, i) -> None:
128	        heap = self._heap
129	        n = len(heap)
130	        while True:
131	            smallest = i
132	            left = 2 * i + 1
133	            right = 2 * i + 2
134	            if left < n and heap[left][0] < heap[smallest][0]:
135	                smallest = left
136	            if right < n and heap[right][0] < heap[smallest][0]:
137	                smallest = right
138	            if smallest != i:
139	                self._swap(i, smallest)
140	                i = smallest
141	            else:
142	                break
143	
144	
145	if __name__ == "__main__":
146	    h = MinHeap()
147	    h.insert("task_c", 30)
148	    h.insert("task_a", 10)
149	    h.insert("task_b", 20)
150	    h.insert("task_d", 40)
151	
152	    print("peek:", h.peek())            # (10, 'task_a')
153	    print("len:", len(h))               # 4
154	    print("contains task_a:", "task_a" in h)  # True
155	
156	    print("extract:", h.extract_min())  # (10, 'task_a')
157	    print("extract:", h.extract_min())  # (20, 'task_b')
158	
159	    h.decrease_key("task_d", 5)
160	    print("after decrease_key(task_d, 5):")
161	    print("extract:", h.extract_min())  # (5, 'task_d')
162	    print("extract:", h.extract_min())  # (30, 'task_c')
163	
164	    # build_heap
165	    h2 = MinHeap([("x", 50), ("y", 10), ("z", 30)])
166	    print("\nbuild_heap extract:", h2.extract_min())  # (10, 'y')
167	
168	    # delete
169	    h3 = MinHeap([("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3)])
170	    h3.delete("b")
171	    print("after delete('b'), extract order:", end=" ")
172	    while h3:
173	        print(h3.extract_min(), end=" ")
174	    print()  # (1, 'a') (3, 'c')
175	
176	    # merge
177	    h4 = MinHeap([("p", 10), ("q", 20)])
178	    h5 = MinHeap([("r", 5), ("s", 15)])
179	    merged = h4.merge(h5)
180	    print("merged extract order:", end=" ")
181	    while merged:
182	        print(merged.extract_min(), end=" ")
183	    print()  # (5, 'r') (10, 'p') (15, 's') (20, 'q')

1	"""Min-heap from scratch with all standard operations.
2	
3	Supports: insert, extract_min, peek, decrease_key, delete,
4	build_heap, merge, and standard dunder methods.
5	"""
6	
7	
8	class MinHeap:
9	    __slots__ = ("_heap", "_pos")
10	
11	    def __init__(self, items=None):
12	        self._heap: list[list] = []  # [key, value] pairs
13	        self._pos: dict = {}  # value -> index in _heap
14	        if items is not None:
15	            self.build_heap(items)
16	
17	    # ── Query ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
18	
19	    def peek(self):
20	        """Return (key, value) of the minimum element. O(1)."""
21	        if not self._heap:
22	            raise IndexError("peek from empty heap")
23	        return tuple(self._heap[0])
24	
25	    def __len__(self) -> int:
26	        return len(self._heap)
27	
28	    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
29	        return bool(self._heap)
30	
31	    def __contains__(self, value) -> bool:
32	        return value in self._pos
33	
34	    # ── Insert ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	
36	    def insert(self, value, key) -> None:
37	        """Insert an item with the given key (priority). O(log n)."""
38	        idx = len(self._heap)
39	        self._heap.append([key, value])
40	        self._pos[value] = idx
41	        self._sift_up(idx)
42	
43	    # ── Extract ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	
45	    def extract_min(self):
46	        """Remove and return (key, value) of the minimum element. O(log n)."""
47	        if not self._heap:
48	            raise IndexError("extract from empty heap")
49	        self._swap(0, len(self._heap) - 1)
50	        key, value = self._heap.pop()
51	        del self._pos[value]
52	        if self._heap:
53	            self._sift_down(0)
54	        return (key, value)
55	
56	    # ── Decrease key ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57	
58	    def decrease_key(self, value, new_key) -> None:
59	        """Decrease the key of the given value. O(log n)."""
60	        if value not in self._pos:
61	            raise KeyError(f"value {value!r} not in heap")
62	        idx = self._pos[value]
63	        if new_key > self._heap[idx][0]:
64	            raise ValueError("new key is greater than current key")
65	        self._heap[idx][0] = new_key
66	        self._sift_up(idx)
67	
68	    # ── Delete ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69	
70	    def delete(self, value) -> None:
71	        """Remove an arbitrary value from the heap. O(log n)."""
72	        if value not in self._pos:
73	            raise KeyError(f"value {value!r} not in heap")
74	        idx = self._pos[value]
75	        last = len(self._heap) - 1
76	        if idx != last:
77	            self._swap(idx, last)
78	            self._heap.pop()
79	            del self._pos[value]
80	            if idx < len(self._heap):
81	                parent = (idx - 1) // 2
82	                if idx > 0 and self._heap[idx][0] < self._heap[parent][0]:
83	                    self._sift_up(idx)
84	                else:
85	                    self._sift_down(idx)
86	        else:
87	            self._heap.pop()
88	            del self._pos[value]
89	
90	    # ── Build heap ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
91	
92	    def build_heap(self, items) -> None:
93	        """Build a heap from an iterable of (value, key) pairs. O(n)."""
94	        self._heap = [[k, v] for v, k in items]
95	        self._pos = {v: i for i, (k, v) in enumerate(self._heap)}
96	        for i in range(len(self._heap) // 2 - 1, -1, -1):
97	            self._sift_down(i)
98	
99	    # ── Merge ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
100	
101	    def merge(self, other: "MinHeap") -> "MinHeap":
102	        """Return a new MinHeap containing elements from both heaps. O(n)."""
103	        combined = []
104	        for key, value in self._heap:
105	            combined.append((value, key))
106	        for key, value in other._heap:
107	            combined.append((value, key))
108	        return MinHeap(combined)
109	
110	    # ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────
111	
112	    def _swap(self, i, j) -> None:
113	        self._heap[i], self._heap[j] = self._heap[j], self._heap[i]
114	        self._pos[self._heap[i][1]] = i
115	        self._pos[self._heap[j][1]] = j
116	
117	    def _sift_up(self, i) -> None:
118	        heap = self._heap
119	        while i > 0:
120	            parent = (i - 1) // 2
121	            if heap[i][0] < heap[parent][0]:
122	                self._swap(i, parent)
123	                i = parent
124	            else:
125	                break
126	
127	    def _sift_down(self, i) -> None:
128	        heap = self._heap
129	        n = len(heap)
130	        while True:
131	            smallest = i
132	            left = 2 * i + 1
133	            right = 2 * i + 2
134	            if left < n and heap[left][0] < heap[smallest][0]:
135	                smallest = left
136	            if right < n and heap[right][0] < heap[smallest][0]:
137	                smallest = right
138	            if smallest != i:
139	                self._swap(i, smallest)
140	                i = smallest
141	            else:
142	                break
143	
144

162	    print("extract:", h.extract_min())  # (30, 'task_c')

166	    print("\nbuild_heap extract:", h2.extract_min())  # (10, 'y')

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import hashlib
4	import math
5	
6	
7	class BloomFilter:
8	    """Space-efficient probabilistic set membership data structure.
9	
10	    Supports false positives (reports an element as present when it is not)
11	    but never false negatives (never misses an element that was added).
12	
13	    Parameters
14	    ----------
15	    capacity : int
16	        Expected maximum number of elements.
17	    error_rate : float
18	        Desired false-positive probability (0 < error_rate < 1).
19	    """
20	
21	    def __init__(self, capacity: int, error_rate: float) -> None:
22	        if capacity <= 0:
23	            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
24	        if not (0 < error_rate < 1):
25	            raise ValueError("error_rate must be between 0 and 1 exclusive")
26	
27	        self.capacity = capacity
28	        self.error_rate = error_rate
29	        self._num_hashes = self._optimal_num_hashes(capacity, error_rate)
30	        self._num_bits = self._optimal_num_bits(capacity, error_rate)
31	        # Use a bytearray for compact storage (1 bit per byte here for
32	        # simplicity; a production filter would pack 8 bits per byte).
33	        self._bits = bytearray(self._num_bits)
34	        self._count = 0
35	
36	    # ---- class-level helpers ----
37	
38	    @staticmethod
39	    def _optimal_num_bits(capacity: int, error_rate: float) -> int:
40	        """m = -(n * ln(p)) / (ln2)^2"""
41	        return int(-capacity * math.log(error_rate) / (math.log(2) ** 2))
42	
43	    @staticmethod
44	    def _optimal_num_hashes(capacity: int, error_rate: float) -> int:
45	        """k = (m/n) * ln2"""
46	        num_bits = BloomFilter._optimal_num_bits(capacity, error_rate)
47	        return max(1, int((num_bits / capacity) * math.log(2)))
48	
49	    @classmethod
50	    def optimal_parameters(cls, capacity: int, error_rate: float) -> dict[str, int]:
51	        """Return the optimal bit-array size and hash count for the given constraints.
52	
53	        Parameters
54	        ----------
55	        capacity : int
56	            Expected number of elements.
57	        error_rate : float
58	            Desired false-positive probability.
59	
60	        Returns
61	        -------
62	        dict with keys ``num_bits`` and ``num_hashes``.
63	        """
64	        num_bits = cls._optimal_num_bits(capacity, error_rate)
65	        num_hashes = cls._optimal_num_hashes(capacity, error_rate)
66	        return {"num_bits": num_bits, "num_hashes": num_hashes}
67	
68	    # ---- internal ----
69	
70	    def _hashes(self, item: str | bytes) -> list[int]:
71	        """Double-hashing scheme: h_i(x) = h1(x) + i * h2(x).
72	
73	        Produces k independent hash positions using only two hash digests.
74	        """
75	        if isinstance(item, str):
76	            item = item.encode("utf-8")
77	
78	        h1 = int.from_bytes(hashlib.md5(item).digest()[:8], "big")
79	        h2 = int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha1(item).digest()[:8], "big")
80	
81	        return [(h1 + i * h2) % self._num_bits for i in range(self._num_hashes)]
82	
83	    # ---- public API ----
84	
85	    def add(self, item: str | bytes) -> None:
86	        """Add an element to the filter."""
87	        if self._count >= self.capacity:
88	            raise OverflowError(
89	                f"BloomFilter is at capacity ({self.capacity}). "
90	                "Adding more elements will degrade the false-positive rate."
91	            )
92	        for idx in self._hashes(item):
93	            self._bits[idx] = 1
94	        self._count += 1
95	
96	    def check(self, item: str | bytes) -> bool:
97	        """Return True if the element *might* be in the set (may be a false positive)."""
98	        return all(self._bits[idx] for idx in self._hashes(item))
99	
100	    def __contains__(self, item: str | bytes) -> bool:
101	        """Check if an element *might* be in the set."""
102	        return self.check(item)
103	
104	    def __len__(self) -> int:
105	        """Number of elements that have been added."""
106	        return self._count
107	
108	    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
109	        return self._count > 0
110	
111	    @property
112	    def num_bits(self) -> int:
113	        return self._num_bits
114	
115	    @property
116	    def num_hashes(self) -> int:
117	        return self._num_hashes
118	
119	    def estimated_fpp(self) -> float:
120	        """Estimated false-positive probability given current fill level."""
121	        if self._count == 0:
122	            return 0.0
123	        return (1 - math.exp(-self._num_hashes * self._count / self._num_bits)) ** self._num_hashes
124	
125	    def merge(self, other: BloomFilter) -> BloomFilter:
126	        """Return a new BloomFilter that is the union of two filters.
127	
128	        Both filters must have identical size and hash parameters.
129	        """
130	        if self._num_bits != other._num_bits:
131	            raise ValueError("Filters must have the same number of bits")
132	        if self._num_hashes != other._num_hashes:
133	            raise ValueError("Filters must use the same number of hash functions")
134	
135	        merged = BloomFilter.__new__(BloomFilter)
136	        merged.capacity = self.capacity + other.capacity
137	        merged.error_rate = min(self.error_rate, other.error_rate)
138	        merged._num_hashes = self._num_hashes
139	        merged._num_bits = self._num_bits
140	        merged._bits = bytearray(a | b for a, b in zip(self._bits, other._bits))
141	        merged._count = self._count + other._count
142	        return merged
143	
144	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
145	        """Serialize the bit array to bytes (packed 8 bits per byte)."""
146	        result = bytearray((self._num_bits + 7) // 8)
147	        for i, bit in enumerate(self._bits):
148	            if bit:
149	                result[i // 8] |= 1 << (i % 8)
150	        return bytes(result)
151	
152	    @classmethod
153	    def from_bytes(cls, data: bytes, capacity: int, error_rate: float) -> BloomFilter:
154	        """Deserialize a filter from packed bytes."""
155	        bf = cls(capacity, error_rate)
156	        for i in range(bf._num_bits):
157	            bf._bits[i] = (data[i // 8] >> (i % 8)) & 1
158	        return bf
159	
160	
161	# ---------- Tests ----------
162	
163	def test_basic_add_and_contains():
164	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
165	    bf.add("hello")
166	    bf.add("world")
167	    assert "hello" in bf
168	    assert "world" in bf
169	    assert "missing" not in bf
170	
171	
172	def test_len():
173	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
174	    assert len(bf) == 0
175	    bf.add("a")
176	    bf.add("b")
177	    assert len(bf) == 2
178	
179	
180	def test_bool():
181	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
182	    assert not bf
183	    bf.add("x")
184	    assert bf
185	
186	
187	def test_bytes_input():
188	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
189	    bf.add(b"\x00\x01\x02")
190	    assert b"\x00\x01\x02" in bf
191	
192	
193	def test_false_positive_rate():
194	    """Inserted items are always found; non-inserted rarely match."""
195	    n = 1000
196	    bf = BloomFilter(n, 0.01)
197	
198	    for i in range(n):
199	        bf.add(f"item-{i}")
200	
201	    # All inserted items must be found (no false negatives)
202	    for i in range(n):
203	        assert f"item-{i}" in bf
204	
205	    # Measure actual false-positive rate on unseen items
206	    false_positives = sum(1 for i in range(n, n * 2) if f"item-{i}" in bf)
207	    fpp = false_positives / n
208	    assert fpp < 0.05, f"False-positive rate {fpp} too high"
209	
210	
211	def test_optimal_parameters():
212	    bf = BloomFilter(1000, 0.01)
213	    assert bf.num_hashes > 0
214	    assert bf.num_bits > 0
215	    # For n=1000, p=0.01: m ~ 9585, k ~ 7
216	    assert bf.num_bits > 5000
217	    assert 3 <= bf.num_hashes <= 15
218	
219	
220	def test_overflow_raises():
221	    bf = BloomFilter(2, 0.01)
222	    bf.add("a")
223	    bf.add("b")
224	    try:
225	        bf.add("c")
226	        assert False, "Expected OverflowError"
227	    except OverflowError:
228	        pass
229	
230	
231	def test_estimated_fpp():
232	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
233	    assert bf.estimated_fpp() == 0.0
234	    bf.add("test")
235	    assert 0 < bf.estimated_fpp() < 1
236	
237	
238	def test_merge():
239	    bf1 = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
240	    bf2 = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
241	    bf1.add("hello")
242	    bf2.add("world")
243	    merged = bf1.merge(bf2)
244	    assert "hello" in merged
245	    assert "world" in merged
246	
247	
248	def test_merge_incompatible():
249	    bf1 = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
250	    bf2 = BloomFilter(200, 0.01)
251	    try:
252	        bf1.merge(bf2)
253	        assert False, "Expected ValueError"
254	    except ValueError:
255	        pass
256	
257	
258	def test_serialization():
259	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
260	    bf.add("alpha")
261	    bf.add("beta")
262	
263	    data = bf.to_bytes()
264	    bf2 = BloomFilter.from_bytes(data, 100, 0.01)
265	    assert "alpha" in bf2
266	    assert "beta" in bf2
267	
268	
269	def test_invalid_params():
270	    try:
271	        BloomFilter(0, 0.01)
272	        assert False
273	    except ValueError:
274	        pass
275	    try:
276	        BloomFilter(100, 0.0)
277	        assert False
278	    except ValueError:
279	        pass
280	    try:
281	        BloomFilter(100, 1.0)
282	        assert False
283	    except ValueError:
284	        pass
285	
286	
287	def test_large_capacity():
288	    bf = BloomFilter(100_000, 0.001)
289	    for i in range(10_000):
290	        bf.add(f"key-{i}")
291	    for i in range(10_000):
292	        assert f"key-{i}" in bf
293	
294	
295	def test_unicode_strings():
296	    bf = BloomFilter(100, 0.01)
297	    bf.add("日本語テスト")
298	    bf.add("émojis 🚀")
299	    assert "日本語テスト" in bf
300	    assert "émojis 🚀" in bf
301	
302	
303	if __name__ == "__main__":
304	    import pytest
305	    pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])

146	        result = bytearray((self._num_bits + 7) // 8)

157	            bf._bits[i] = (data[i // 8] >> (i % 8)) & 1
158	        return bf

1	"""Trie-based hierarchical metrics aggregation.
2	
3	Collects counters, gauges, and histograms keyed by dot-separated metric names
4	(e.g. ``"http.requests.total"``).  Each trie node aggregates the metrics of
5	its subtree, so ``range_query`` over a prefix is efficient.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
11	from enum import Enum
12	from typing import Any
13	
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# Metric types
17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	
19	class MetricType(Enum):
20	    """Supported metric types."""
21	    COUNTER = "counter"
22	    GAUGE = "gauge"
23	    HISTOGRAM = "histogram"
24	
25	
26	@dataclass
27	class Counter:
28	    """Monotonically increasing counter."""
29	    value: float = 0.0
30	
31	    def update(self, amount: float) -> None:
32	        self.value += amount
33	
34	    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
35	        return {"type": "counter", "value": self.value}
36	
37	
38	@dataclass
39	class Gauge:
40	    """Gauge that can go up or down; stores the latest value."""
41	    value: float = 0.0
42	
43	    def update(self, amount: float) -> None:
44	        self.value = amount
45	
46	    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
47	        return {"type": "gauge", "value": self.value}
48	
49	
50	@dataclass
51	class Histogram:
52	    """Histogram with fixed bucket boundaries.
53	
54	    Default buckets suit latency measurements in milliseconds.  Pass
55	    custom ``boundaries`` for other ranges.
56	    """
57	    boundaries: tuple[float, ...] = (1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000)
58	    buckets: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
59	    count: int = 0
60	    sum: float = 0.0
61	
62	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
63	        if not self.buckets:
64	            self.buckets = [0] * (len(self.boundaries) + 1)
65	
66	    def update(self, value: float) -> None:
67	        self.count += 1
68	        self.sum += value
69	        for i, boundary in enumerate(self.boundaries):
70	            if value <= boundary:
71	                self.buckets[i] += 1
72	                return
73	        self.buckets[-1] += 1  # overflow bucket
74	
75	    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
76	        return {
77	            "type": "histogram",
78	            "count": self.count,
79	            "sum": self.sum,
80	            "mean": self.sum / self.count if self.count else 0.0,
81	            "buckets": dict(zip(
82	                [str(b) for b in self.boundaries] + ["+Inf"],
83	                self.buckets,
84	            )),
85	        }
86	
87	
88	# Aggregation accumulator used during range_query.
89	@dataclass
90	class _AggResult:
91	    counters: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
92	    gauges: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
93	    histograms: dict[str, Histogram] = field(default_factory=dict)
94	
95	    def merge_counter(self, name: str, c: Counter) -> None:
96	        self.counters[name] = self.counters.get(name, 0.0) + c.value
97	
98	    def merge_gauge(self, name: str, g: Gauge) -> None:
99	        self.gauges[name] = self.gauges.get(name, 0.0) + g.value
100	
101	    def merge_histogram(self, name: str, h: Histogram) -> None:
102	        if name not in self.histograms:
103	            self.histograms[name] = Histogram(boundaries=h.boundaries)
104	        agg = self.histograms[name]
105	        agg.count += h.count
106	        agg.sum += h.sum
107	        for i in range(len(agg.buckets)):
108	            agg.buckets[i] += h.buckets[i]
109	
110	
111	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
112	# TrieNode
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	
115	class TrieNode:
116	    """A trie node that stores hierarchical metrics.
117	
118	    Metric names are split on ``"."``; each segment becomes a child link.
119	    Leaf nodes hold the actual metric values while every node in the path
120	    maintains an aggregate of its subtree for fast ``range_query``.
121	
122	    Args:
123	        separator: Delimiter used to split metric names (default ``"."``).
124	
125	    Example::
126	
127	        root = TrieNode()
128	        root.insert("http.requests.total", 1, MetricType.COUNTER)
129	        root.insert("http.requests.total", 3, MetricType.COUNTER)
130	        root.insert("http.latency.p99", 42.5, MetricType.GAUGE)
131	
132	        snap = root.range_query("http.")
133	        # snap.counters == {"http.requests.total": 4.0}
134	        # snap.gauges   == {"http.latency.p99": 42.5}
135	    """
136	
137	    __slots__ = ("children", "counters", "gauges", "histograms", "_separator")
138	
139	    def __init__(self, separator: str = ".") -> None:
140	        self.children: dict[str, TrieNode] = {}
141	        self.counters: dict[str, Counter] = {}
142	        self.gauges: dict[str, Gauge] = {}
143	        self.histograms: dict[str, Histogram] = {}
144	        self._separator = separator
145	
146	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
147	    # Core operations
148	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
149	
150	    def insert(
151	        self,
152	        name: str,
153	        value: float,
154	        metric_type: MetricType,
155	        *,
156	        boundaries: tuple[float, ...] | None = None,
157	    ) -> None:
158	        """Insert a metric value into the trie.
159	
160	        Args:
161	            name: Dot-separated metric name (e.g. ``"cpu.usage"``).
162	            value: Numeric value.  For counters this is the *delta* to add;
163	                for gauges it is the new absolute value; for histograms it is
164	                an observation to record.
165	            metric_type: One of ``MetricType.COUNTER``, ``GAUGE``, or
166	                ``HISTOGRAM``.
167	            boundaries: Custom histogram bucket boundaries.  Only used when
168	                *metric_type* is ``HISTOGRAM`` and the metric is created for
169	                the first time.
170	        """
171	        parts = name.split(self._separator)
172	        node = self
173	        for part in parts:
174	            if part not in node.children:
175	                node.children[part] = TrieNode(separator=self._separator)
176	            node = node.children[part]
177	
178	        if metric_type is MetricType.COUNTER:
179	            if name not in node.counters:
180	                node.counters[name] = Counter()
181	            node.counters[name].update(value)
182	        elif metric_type is MetricType.GAUGE:
183	            if name not in node.gauges:
184	                node.gauges[name] = Gauge()
185	            node.gauges[name].update(value)
186	        elif metric_type is MetricType.HISTOGRAM:
187	            if name not in node.histograms:
188	                node.histograms[name] = Histogram(
189	                    boundaries=boundaries or Histogram().boundaries,
190	                )
191	            node.histograms[name].update(value)
192	
193	    def delete(self, name: str) -> bool:
194	        """Remove a metric entirely from the trie.
195	
196	        Args:
197	            name: The full dot-separated metric name to delete.
198	
199	        Returns:
200	            ``True`` if the metric was found and removed, ``False`` otherwise.
201	        """
202	        parts = name.split(self._separator)
203	        path: list[tuple[TrieNode, str]] = []
204	        node = self
205	        for part in parts:
206	            if part not in node.children:
207	                return False
208	            path.append((node, part))
209	            node = node.children[part]
210	
211	        removed = False
212	        if name in node.counters:
213	            del node.counters[name]
214	            removed = True
215	        if name in node.gauges:
216	            del node.gauges[name]
217	            removed = True
218	        if name in node.histograms:
219	            del node.histograms[name]
220	            removed = True
221	
222	        if not removed:
223	            return False
224	
225	        # Prune empty leaf nodes bottom-up.
226	        for parent, key in reversed(path):
227	            child = parent.children[key]
228	            if (
229	                not child.children
230	                and not child.counters
231	                and not child.gauges
232	                and not child.histograms
233	            ):
234	                del parent.children[key]
235	            else:
236	                break
237	
238	        return True
239	
240	    def range_query(self, prefix: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
241	        """Aggregate all metrics whose name starts with *prefix*.
242	
243	        Args:
244	            prefix: A dot-separated prefix (e.g. ``"http."``).  An empty
245	                string matches every metric in the trie.
246	
247	        Returns:
248	            A dict with three keys:
249	
250	            - ``"counters"`` – ``{name: summed_value, ...}``
251	            - ``"gauges"`` – ``{name: latest_value, ...}``
252	            - ``"histograms"`` – ``{name: merged_histogram_snapshot, ...}``
253	        """
254	        agg = _AggResult()
255	        node = self._find(prefix)
256	        if node is not None:
257	            self._collect(node, prefix, agg)
258	        return {
259	            "counters": agg.counters,
260	            "gauges": agg.gauges,
261	            "histograms": {
262	                name: h.snapshot() for name, h in agg.histograms.items()
263	            },
264	        }
265	
266	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
267	    # Introspection helpers
268	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
269	
270	    def get(self, name: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
271	        """Return the raw snapshot for a single metric, or ``None``."""
272	        parts = name.split(self._separator)
